key: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope.
s: Near the surah’s close, after the warning that hidden thoughts will be reckoned, comes this assurance; al-Tabari, on 2:286, reads it as Allah never overtaxing a soul in its religion, nor holding it to account for an intention, a whispered suggestion or a passing thought.

evidence.words: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: لا يكلف الله نفسا فيتعبدها إلا بما يسعها، فلا يضيق عليها ولا يجهدها … فتأويل الآية إذا: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما يسعها فلا يجهدها، ولا يضيق عليها في أمر دينها، فيؤاخذها بهمة إن همت، ولا بوسوسة إن عرضت لها، ولا بخطرة إن خطرت بقلبها
evidence.gloss: He means by it: God does not burden a soul, binding it to His service, except with what is within its capacity, so He does not constrain it or overtax it … The meaning of the ayah, then, is: God burdens no soul except with what it can bear, so He does not overtax it nor constrain it in the matter of its religion by taking it to account for an intention if it intends, a whispering if one comes to it, or a passing thought if one crosses its heart.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Baqarah 2:286, at 292). Plain sense faithful: the day ends with 2:284 (whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide it, Allah will bring you to account), 2:285 and 2:286; the context clause names 2:284 without a four-word run from the key. In the packet on 2:286 al-Tabari glosses the clause as God binding no soul to His service beyond its capacity, reports Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi tying it to the believers’ distress over inner whisperings, and sums up the ayah as God not taking a soul to account for an intention, a whispering or a passing thought. The sentence carries his own summary without drift. Evidence cut by script from the packet text. Entry-check ok.
